claims.text: MOUs: 1999 (FY1999–2008) $26.7bn incl $21.3bn military; 2007 (FY2009–18) $30bn, up to 26.3% offshore procurement; 2016 (signed 14 Sep 2016, FY2019–28) $38bn = $33bn FMF + $5bn missile defense, OSP phased out.

Naval Vessel Transfer Act 2008 (P.L. 110-429) defined QME, required QME assessment every four years, amended AECA so other Mideast sales cannot adversely affect Israel's QME. US-Israel Strategic Partnership Act (P.L. 113-296) amended AECA s.36.

FY1987 NDAA (P.L. 99-661, 4 Nov 1986) s.1105 created major non-NATO ally category; Israel designated Feb 1987. P.L. 101-513 (FY1991) required Israel's FMF be disbursed as lump sum in first month (early disbursement), held in interest-bearing account at the Federal Reserve. Emergency Security Assistance Act 1973 (P.L. 93-199) $2.2bn. FAA s.516(a) EDA eligibility. AECA s.23 cash flow financing.
FY2021 NDAA s.1273 authorizes not less than $3.3bn FMF annually through 2028. P.L. 119-4 (FY2025): loan guarantees reauthorized through 2030; WRSA additions cap $500m/yr through FY2027; $450.3m OSP.
Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act 2024 (P.L. 118-50, April 2024): $3.5bn FMF, $4bn missile defense, $1.2bn Iron Beam. Missile defense FY2024 total $5.7bn.

Cumulative US aid to Israel 1946–2025: about $174bn current dollars (~$298bn in 2024 dollars). Cooperative programs FY2025: counter-tunnel $47.5m, counter-UAS $55m, emerging tech $20m. FY2025 NDAA s.1213 joint exercises incl subterranean, s.1214 DIU partnership.

Since Oct 2023: Iron Dome batteries from US Army stock; Aug 2024 FMS >$20bn incl F-15IA; Feb 2025 $8.4bn notifications and 28 Feb 2025 emergency declaration (AECA 36(b)) ~$4bn bypassing review; Apr 2025 751 active FMS cases worth $39.2bn; Israel MoD: 800 planes and 140 ships delivered 90,000+ tons by May 2025. S.Res. 504 (Dec 2023) seeking 502B human rights report failed.

30 Nov 1981 Strategic Cooperation MOU, Weinberger and Sharon: joint committee for exercises, Sixth Fleet use of Israeli ports, pre-positioning US supplies in Israel, cluster bomb deliveries resumed, +$425m/yr; executive MOU not subject to Senate ratification; reconfirmed 21 Apr 1988.

US-Israel Enhanced Security Cooperation Act 2012: Sen. Boxer, 71 co-sponsors, Senate unanimous voice vote 29 Jun 2012; signed by Obama 27 Jul 2012; extended WRSA-I authority and loan guarantees; called for Iron Dome support; US policy to help preserve Israel's QME; QME report in 180 days.

US-Israel Strategic Partnership Act 2014: Boxer and Blunt; Senate unanimous 18 Sep 2014, House voice vote 3 Dec 2014; sense of Congress Israel is a 'major strategic partner'; extends WRSA authority; visa waiver policy; homeland security research pilots (border, maritime, aviation security); cyber cooperation report; energy/water cooperation.
15 Jan 2021 Pentagon moved Israel from EUCOM to CENTCOM in Unified Command Plan; WSJ: Trump ordered it; Pentagon: 'the Abraham Accords paved the way'; IDF liaison officers at CENTCOM HQ in Tampa.

27 Sep 2023 DHS/State designated Israel in Visa Waiver Program (ESTA from 30 Nov 2023) after Israel's 19 Jul 2023 reciprocity commitments covering all US citizens incl. Palestinian Americans; Blinken quote.

claims.text: Rusk's review of 7 Aug 1962 recommended offering the Hawk if no arms-limitation deal with Egypt looked likely; Feldman carried the decision to Ben-Gurion and Meir in August 1962; Circular 1008 (7 Sep 1962) called the Hawk purely defensive; sale on US credit; first deliveries by early 1965.
Rusk told Lord Hood that Feldman was 'in no sense attempting to close a Hawk deal'; a sale was open in principle 'subject to the possibility of arms control arrangements' (19 Aug 1962 memo).

Johnson signed the Foreign Assistance Act of 1968 on 9 Oct 1968 noting its section on plane sales to Israel; Senate sense-of-Congress resolution of July 1968; sale of 50 Phantoms announced 27 Dec 1968; $285m; 16 delivered late 1969, 34 in 1970.

Rabin's 22 Nov 1968 letter: Israel 'will not be the first power in the Middle East to introduce nuclear weapons' and would not use US-supplied aircraft as nuclear carriers; US reserved right to cancel in 'unusual and compelling circumstances'.
Operation Nickel Grass: 14 Oct–14 Nov 1973, 32 days, about 22,300 tons delivered.

Nixon on 19 Oct 1973 asked Congress for $2.2bn emergency security assistance for Israel to maintain 'a balance of military capabilities' against 'a large-scale resupply of Syria and Egypt by the Soviet Union'.

P.L. 93-199 (26 Dec 1973) authorized up to $2.2bn for Israel; above $1.5bn required presidential determination and 20-day report; s.4 allowed release of Israel from liability to pay for arms bought 6 Oct 1973–30 Jun 1974.
Senate passed H.R. 11088 66–9 on 20 Dec 1973 and tabled Fulbright's amendment tying aid above $1.2bn to steps toward compliance with Resolution 242, 62–12.

September 1975 US–Israel Memorandum of Agreement (with Sinai II): oil-supply guarantee for five years; US to view Israel's arms requests 'sympathetically'; US will not recognize or negotiate with the PLO 'so long as' it does not recognize Israel's right to exist and accept 242 and 338.
US recognized Israel's provisional government as de facto authority on 14 May 1948; de jure recognition 31 Jan 1949.

claims.text: MOU signed 30 Nov 1981 by Weinberger and Sharon; Knesset passed Golan Heights Law 14 Dec 1981; US suspended the MOU 18 Dec 1981; not reinstated until 17 May 1983.
Begin said Israel understood the suspension to mean cancellation (CSM, 21 Dec 1981).
6 May 1986 secret agreement for Israeli participation in SDI research; Arrow developed under SDI; 1989 agreement (Rabin–Cheney) allowed pre-positioning up to $100m US supplies in Israel.
21 Apr 1988 MOA signed by Shamir and Reagan: notes MNNA designation under s.1105 FY1987 NDAA; creates JPMG, JSAP, JEDG; five-year renewable term.
US–Israel FTA entered into force 1985, 'the United States' first FTA'; 2024 US exports $14.8bn, imports $22.2bn.
WRSA-I: April 1984 MOU inaugurated pre-positioning; Sept 1989 decision; $100m in 1989; reported $1.2bn by 2020; drawdowns 2006 and 2014 with US permission; Congress sets annual value of additions.
NPR 2014: stockpile of roughly $1bn established in 1980s; Israel can use it only with US approval; Pentagon allowed tank shells and illumination rounds in July 2014.
BIRD Foundation established by US and Israeli governments 1977 (ceremony 18 May 1977); endowment $60m raised to $110m in 1984, equal contributions; 900+ projects, ~$10bn sales.

Once disbursed (within 30 days of enactment), Israel's FMF goes to an interest-bearing account at the Federal Reserve; interest previously used to pay bilateral debt; Israel cannot use interest for procurement inside Israel; no outstanding sovereign debt to US as of Sept 2024. 1973 $2.2bn allocated $1.5bn grants/$700m loans. Israel's share of global FMF roughly 40% (Shapiro).
29 Nov 1983 Reagan–Shamir meeting revived strategic cooperation and created a Joint Political-Military Group.

claims.text: 2016 MOU: FY2019–28, $38bn ($33bn FMF + $5bn missile defense; $3.3bn + $500m a year); ends the 26.3% OSP allowance and FMF fuel purchases, meaning up to $1.2bn more a year spent on US-made capabilities; 'largest single pledge of military assistance in U.S. history'; US capabilities the best way for Israel to maintain QME.

Iron Dome US funding FY2011 $205m, FY2012 $70m, FY2013 $194m, FY2014 $235.3m + $225m supplemental = $929.3m; March 2014 coproduction agreement allows US manufacture of components and gives MDA full access to previously proprietary Iron Dome technology; Raytheon $149m Tamir parts contract 30 Sep 2014.
Arrow 2 first deployed 2000; Arrow 3 fielded 2017; David's Sling development from 2006, fielded 2017; Iron Dome first fielded 2011.

Counter-tunnel cooperation authorized by s.1279 FY2016 NDAA (P.L. 114-92), counter-UAS by s.1278 FY2020 NDAA; WRSA authority in s.12001 of DoD Appropriations Act 2005 (P.L. 108-287); S.554 (Feb 2025) would raise caps to $80m and $75m, extend to 2028 and add $50m/yr emerging-tech cooperation.
DHS S&T–Israel MOPS binational pilot under the 2009 US–Israel agreement on homeland security S&T cooperation; began 2016, became BIRD HLS 2019; $9.65m public funds, 10 projects.
House passed standalone $1bn Iron Dome replenishment 420–9 on 23 Sep 2021 after it was removed from a stopgap bill.
House passed H.R. 8034 366–58 on 20 Apr 2024 (R 193–21, D 173–37); Senate 79–18 on 23 Apr 2024; signed 24 Apr 2024 as P.L. 118-50.

Rubio 1 Mar 2025 signed declaration using emergency authorities to expedite ~$4bn military assistance; nearly $12bn FMS approved since inauguration; criticized Biden's 'partial arms embargo' and NSM-20 conditions.
Israel MOD 5 Jun 2026: talks launched on framework to replace MOU expiring 2028, to 'gradually transition from aid to a completely reciprocal partnership'; teams Baram/Leiter and Holler/Huckabee.

Jan 2026 reports Netanyahu seeks to end US military aid within 10 years; 1 Jun 2026 letter to Rep. Stutzman 'move from aid recipient to partner'; July 2026 Israel pushing to accelerate talks; no concluded agreement reported.
Susskind (president of New Jewish Narrative) argues the proposed framework would fold support into Pentagon procurement, leaving 'no annual appropriation to debate' and 'no line item to block'.
